message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant genetic traits is the **presence of a mane** in adult males. The gene(s) responsible for mane growth are expressed dominantly, meaning that a single copy of the allele is sufficient for a male lion to develop a full mane. This trait is typically absent in females and in male cubs until puberty, when the dominant allele triggers the growth of the mane.
